newsitem.title: USA: Florida man seeks to lift stay on assisted suicide.
newsitem.headline: Florida man seeks to lift stay on assisted suicide.

text.p: A dying AIDS patient seeking to win the legal right to physician-assisted suicide asked a judge Monday to lift a stay preventing him from taking his own life.

Last week Palm Beach County Judge Joseph Davis ruled Charles Hall had the right to take his own life with the assistance of a doctor. But the state of Florida, which had opposed Hall, immediately announced it would appeal, triggering a 30-day stay.
In a motion filed by his attorney, Robert Rivas, Hall asked Circuit Judge Lucy Brown to set aside the stay. A hearing on the motion was scheduled for Tuesday.

Hall, 35, who was bedridden at his Beverly Hills, Florida, home, was being treated for his fourth bout of AIDS-related pneumonia. Jupiter physician Cecil McIver, who agreed to help Hall end his life should the courts allow it, described Hall as "a very sick man."

In seeking to lift the stay Rivas said Hall "suffered almost a year of continuing anxiety and frustration in an effort to obtain the peace of mind afforded to him by knowing that he has choices available to him in the manner of his death."
Rivas said the state's appeal "robbed him of these choices."

"Whatever the public policy arguments in support of the automatic stay in other cases, they have no weight here," Rivas said. "Mr. Hall is ... entitled to the benefits of (Judge Davis' decision), and the state has no legitimate interest in denying him its benefits during the appeal."
Hall sued Florida in February 1996, asking that McIver be spared from prosecution for helping him end his life if his pain became intolerable.
On Friday Davis entered an order forbidding the local state attorney from filing any criminal action against McIver, as well as anyone who might assist him in helping Hall end his life.
Davis stressed in his order that the ruling applied only to Hall and McIver and would not carry weight in other cases.
